subtype: Approach: keeps studying the same way despite poor results [Pitfall]
passage:
Dear Chandrika,
Results came out. Chemistry, 41 out of 100, again. I don't get it. I sat with the notes for five hours the night before and read every page twice, highlighting in three colours.
Amma says maybe I should try some other way, but rereading is what I have done since class six and it feels like real studying. At night everything looked familiar, so I was sure I knew it. Then the paper asked me to explain things and my mind went blank.
The next exam is in three weeks. I think I'll start earlier and reread more.
Write back soon.
Ashwin

qa.q: How long did Ashwin sit with the notes the night before the paper?
qa.a: Ashwin sat with the notes for five hours and read every page twice.

qa.q: What does Ashwin feel about the way of studying used so far?
qa.a: Ashwin feels attached to rereading and trusts it, saying it feels like real studying even though the marks stayed low.

qa.q: What different approach could Ashwin try before the next exam, and why?
qa.a: Ashwin could close the notes and test by answering questions from memory, since the paper asked for explanations and rereading only made the pages look familiar.

qa.q: How might Amma feel about the plan to reread more?
qa.a: Amma already suggested some other way, so may feel worried that Ashwin will repeat what has not worked.

grounding: A student rereads notes for hours, scores poorly and does not try self-testing because rereading is the habit.
